fact: The Uganda Police Force says its ICT Directorate has developed a crime records system for the Directorate of Crime Investigations that processes and tracks the progress of case files and eases the monitoring and management of crimes reported; no date is given beyond the document's publication, 14 December 2017.

The Uganda Police Force says the finalised crime records system was being piloted in ten divisions of Kampala Metropolitan, with no total of divisions or stations given; dated by the document's publication, 14 December 2017.

The Uganda Police Force says the crime records system was developed by its own ICT Directorate through the force's ICT Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship Excellence, set up in 2014 by the Inspector General of Police in partnership with Microsoft; dated by the document's publication, 14 December 2017.

The Uganda Police Force names no budget line or funder for the crime records system, and says licence renewal and funds are among the greatest challenges of the police centre that built it, with NITA promising to help negotiate them; dated by the document's publication, 14 December 2017.

The article states that the Uganda Police Force's Electronic Policing Information System, through which a crime case management system is being developed to manage all cases registered and investigated by the police from inception to conclusion countrywide, is in its design phase; no station is said to use it, and no date is given beyond the article's publication, 10 June 2024.

The article states that the crime case management system being developed through ePIS is primarily owned by the Uganda Police Force's Directorate of Criminal Investigations, with stakeholders across the criminal justice chain taking part in the design; dated by the article's publication, 10 June 2024.

A senior officer of the Uganda Police Force's ICT directorate writes that the force resolved in October 2022 to embark on the Electronic Policing Information System project, and the head of the legal department of its Criminal Investigations Directorate writes that the Inspector General and all heads of directorates have endorsed the project, which seeks to automate case management processes across the force.

The bulletin's two police articles describe ePIS throughout as a project that 'seeks to' automate case management across the force and 'will' share data with prosecutors, courts and prisons; neither says it is in use at any station, and the editorial lists lack of internet connectivity at upcountry police stations among the obstacles; dated by the bulletin's imprint, May 2024.

The Inspector General of Police states that in 2024 the force plans to strengthen its business and case management systems under the ePIS project, which he calls an integrated digital platform for the management of policing services, and to embrace paperless transactions through ICT systems in all 29 regions.
The Inspector General of Police names no budget line or funder for the ePIS project in his message of 22 December 2023.

The Independent reports that the Uganda Police Force's digital Crime Record Management System replaces a manual system based on moving copies of hard case files, and is used by the records officers at police stations; the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.

The Independent reports, quoting the police ICT directorate's spokesman, that the system was pioneered in Kampala Metropolitan in 2017, stalled when station records officers found it hard to use, has been upgraded and tested in Kampala, is to be tested in upcountry stations next, and will be rolled out only once the Police Advisory Committee accepts it; no count of stations is given, and the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.

The Independent reports that police stations currently have one records officer in charge of case files and that detectives therefore keep the files of the cases they handle, the digital system not yet being rolled out; the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.
